summary: James Mallinson is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. Educated at Eton, SOAS, and Oxford (D.Phil. 2003 under Alexis Sanderson), he lectured at SOAS (2013) before becoming Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit in 2023, succeeding Christopher Minkowski.

James Mark Shields works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. In 2016, he was attested as an Associate Professor of Comparative Humanities and Asian Thought at Bucknell University and an Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.
James Matthew Baskind is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. at Yale University under the supervision of Stanley Weinstein (attested 2006).

James McHugh is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Cambridge, Oxford, and Harvard (PhD), working with teachers including Lawrence J. McCrea, Anne E. Monius, and Parimal G. Patil. He held posts at the University of Southern California and Cornell.

James Miller is a sinologist and religious studies scholar. He earned an M.A. from Cambridge (1997) and a Ph.D. from Boston University (2000), and was attested in 2014 as Professor of Chinese Studies and Religious Studies at Queen's University Belfast.
James Morison was an Indology scholar who studied under Georg Bühler. He served as a librarian at the University of Oxford (attested 1917–1920).

James Murdoch (1856–1921) was a scholar of Japanology and history. He studied at Aberdeen (~1874–1879) and under Theodor Benfey (~1878–1879), and held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1890–1893), Kanazawa University (~1898–1901), and Kagoshima University (~1901–1908).

James Prinsep (1799–1840) was an Indologist and historian. A Royal Society Fellow (1828), he worked at the Benares and Kolkata mints, founded the Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal, and headed The Asiatic Society (1832–1838) after Horace Hayman Wilson.

James R. Ballantyne (1813–1864) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. Educated at Edinburgh and under James Michael and Francis Johnson, he served as master at the Scottish Naval and Military Academy, principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and India Office librarian.

James Robson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Educated at UC Santa Barbara and Stanford (PhD 2002), he held posts at Williams, Michigan, and Harvard, becoming Harvard-Yenching Institute director in 2024, succeeding Elizabeth J. Perry.

James Santucci is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He served as Professor of Religion at California State University (attested 1998) and Chair and Professor of Comparative Religion at California State University, Fullerton (attested 2007).

James Smith Reid (1846–1926) was an archaeological historian who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1865–1869). He held academic posts at Christ's College (1869–1880), Pembroke College (1873–1885), and Gonville and Caius College (1878–1926).

James Sutherland Cotton (1847–1918) was an Indologist and historian educated at Winchester, Brighton, Magdalen College School, and Trinity College, Oxford. He held posts at Queens' College, Cambridge, and The Queen's College, Oxford, where he was Fellow and Lecturer (1871–1874).

James Tod (1782–1835) was a historian and Indologist trained at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich, who studied under Gyanchandra. He served with the East India Company (~1799–1823) and as Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1835).
James W. Benson is an Indologist and linguist. He held appointments as Assistant Professor in Sanskrit at Harvard University (attested 1999–2003) and at Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2004).

James W. Heisig is a philosopher and religious studies scholar. Educated at Divine Word, Loyola, Notre Dame, and Cambridge (PhD 1973), he was a permanent research fellow at Nanzan University from ~1974 and served as director from 1991 to 2001.

James Ward (1843–1925) was a philosopher. He studied at Mostyn House School, Fitzwilliam College, and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1869–1874), and held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from ~1897 to 1925.
James Whitehill is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He founded the Columbia Zen Center and was attested as Professor of Religion at Stephens College in 2000.

James Wilson Bright (1852–1926) was a linguist educated at Lafayette College and Johns Hopkins University (PhD ~1882). He taught briefly at Cornell (~1885) and held the Caroline Donovan Chair of English at Johns Hopkins from 1905 to 1925.

Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso (1846–1912) was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar and philosopher. He studied under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, and Patrul Rinpoche, and instructed numerous disciples such as Shechen Gyaltsab and Khenpo Shenga.
